final.title: When AI gives wrong answers, narrow the workflow
final.body:
If you run a one-person business, the real problem is not that AI sounds confident. It is that it can drift outside the process you actually trust. That is a control problem, not a personality problem.

The useful question is simple: can this task be bounded by material you already trust? I mean your own documents, past answers, rules, or procedures. If yes, the AI should look there before it answers. In plain terms, that is a grounded workflow: it retrieves relevant approved company material instead of reaching for the open web. That does not eliminate bad answers, but it does narrow the room for invention.

So use one diagnostic question: “Do I have a pile of answers, documents, or procedures I already trust, and am I asking the AI to answer only from that pile?” If the answer is yes, the next step is a small pilot inside your own environment, using your own data and tools, with code and accounts kept in your name. That scope is a target, not a promise.

If the answer is no, or you are still unsure, keep the task manual for now or consider hiring. That is often the cleaner choice than asking a model to improvise where precision matters. The machine can wait; the workflow should not.
